semanticDecisions: the stock lanes alone decide: the regionMatchesCI family says whether a window matches and the compareToCI family words the first window that differs; the mismatch front is exact because the stock rule folds from the first differing unit on, a Latin-1 unit on its own and a low surrogate together with the high surrogate before it, equal on both sides, where the fold restarts one unit earlier

a window of two UTF-16 sides is cut where neither side has a high surrogate before the cut and a low surrogate after it, the unit after the window fetched for that; A28 moved the cut back once when a side ended with a high surrogate, which could split the other side's pair and fold its low unit alone (the new test fails on the A40 build at a 256-unit Deseret text, compareToIgnoreCase -10239 against the flat 1); when every cut of a window splits a pair (pairs misaligned by one unit on both sides, both ways), the window takes the rest of the range as one, bounded by the strings

a residual of the stock code-point rule stays: against a lone high surrogate followed by a pair on one side and a pair on the other, the stock loop folds the shared high twice and continues one unit apart on the two sides; a window reproduces that within itself and a later window restarts the two sides together, which can differ from the stock word only when the two texts, one unit apart, stay equal across a whole window

an M3 side keeps one transient window per side, grown with the graded windows (64, 256, 1024, 4096 units) and reused; a flat side is never copied except as the exact-length tail of the window that differs
mixed coders keep the stock regionMatchesCI_UTF16 / regionMatchesCI_Latin1 loops over the window, whose per-unit equality test is their own fast path
